text:
Alex: kicked off an nsys capture on the nightly batcher run, qdrep at /tmp/nsys/batcher_pinned_qdrep
Sanjay: what symptom are we chasing?
Alex: small-req p90 spiked from ~60ms to ~320ms after yesterday's batching changes
Jessie: uploaded timeline screenshot: https://files.internal/traceshots/1951239999.png
Maria: looking at the timeline: long contiguous H2D memcpy blocks on the default stream, GPU idle while host memcpy runs
Alex: memcpy sizes ~1MB per request, shows as a single host copy syscall region in the CPU timeline
Sanjay: do we see async copies or sync fallbacks? any pinned alloc failures in the trace?
Alex: NVTX + stack samples show the prefetch path falling back to sync path frequently; the pinned allocator pool had exhaustion spikes
Jessie: code excerpt from prefetcher (simplified):
```
if (!got_pinned) {
  cudaMemcpy(dst, src, sz, cudaMemcpyHostToDevice); // sync fallback
} else {
  cudaMemcpyAsync(dst, src, sz, memcpy_stream);
}
```
Maria: so when pinned fails we block the scheduling thread in cudaMemcpy, delaying enqueue of the SPMM kernel -> explains the gap
Alex: interestingly, there are a couple of D2D memcpy kernels that execute between our main kernels; NVTX labels them as "cache-migrate"
Sanjay: my theory: batching heuristic increased prefetch fanout; pinned pool thrashes -> sync fallbacks -> host CPU stays stuck on memcpy -> kernel enqueue gets delayed and kernel selection changes (we pick larger tile kernel later)
Jessie: I ran a local quick test: disabling prefetch for tiny prefixes returned p90 to ~65ms
Maria: perf counters: PCIe bandwidth spikes line up with those memcpy blocks, SM utilization near zero during them
Alex: repro command I used to capture trace:
```
nsys profile --output=batcher_pinned --trace=cuda,osrt,alloc --capture-range=nvtx --sample=cpu --target-processes=all --duration=25s
```
Sanjay: let's try variants across instance types (different drivers/PCIe engines) and with a dedicated memcpy stream bound to a copy engine
Jessie: note: some older drivers may serialize host-driven copies with kernels unless we use the async copy engine correctly and keep streams non-default
Maria: short-term mitigation: reduce prefetch aggressiveness and increase pinned pool size in staging to validate
Alex: longer-term fixes: 1) instrument pinned allocator (counters + NVTX) 2) make async fallback path that stages into pinned buffers on a separate worker thread 3) add batcher guardrail to avoid switching kernel variants when enqueue latency > threshold
Jessie: I'll add a canary config flip to staging to lower prefetch and run smoke traces tomorrow morning
Sanjay: action items assigned: SANJ-alloc (pinned allocator NVTX), MAR-batcher (prefetch metrics + sync-fallback telemetry), JES-repro (small-req repro + multi-flavor nsys captures)
Alex: also capture traces with stream priorities set and with/without a dedicated memcpy stream to see if copy engine behavior changes
Maria: created tickets: INFR-694 (prefetch telemetry), INFR-695 (pinned allocator NVTX), PERF-520 (batcher heuristic guardrails)
Jessie: drop any additional qdreps here from other instance types, helps rule out driver vs code
Sanjay: good plan :thumbsup:
